sentences.text: The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(1)93/L&B/LA/3831 dtd. 04.06.2004 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 72 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (1)/93/L&B/LA/2626 dtd.
03.06.2005 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 72 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Pooth Kalan, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 04 of 200607 dated 20.10.2006 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 72 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 14 4.

It is stated that the petitioners are recorded owner/ cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no.
19/23/2 Min (40) and 34//3 (416) in which petitioner no. 1 to 5 are having 1/7th share each,
petitioner no. 6 and 7 having 1/14th share each and petitioner no.8 to 10 having 1/21 share each,
situated in the revenue estate of Village Pooth Kalan, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the petitioners have neither received any kind of notice U/s 9 and 10 of LA Act,
1894 from the office of LAC nor given any hearing to the objection filed by the petitioner under Section 5A of LA Act.

It is further submitted that the award was pronounced by the LAC on 20.10.2006, but neither any notice whatsoever regarding the pronouncement of the award has been given to the petitioners, the petitioner could not come to know of the pronouncement of the award and contents of the award.

Further, the petitioners challenged the award dated 20.10.2006 by filing a Writ petition which was disposed off by the Hon'ble High Court on 07.05.2007 and thereafter the petitioners are filed the present reference petition.

6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.

The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No.
04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The acquired land of the petitioners is situated in the middle of fully developed residential colony namely Rohini.

The acquired land of the petitioners falls in Sector 22 of Residential Scheme and the same is situated at 30 mtrs wide main road connecting the NH10 through main KanjhawalaBawana Road and the same also leads to NH1.
The area in which the land of the petitioners situated having a great importance commercially as well as residentially.

The Sector22 is a fully developed sector and at the date of notification U/s 4 in respect of the land of the petitioners the sector was fully developed and the DDA had itself auctioned various plots of land in Sector22 as well as other adjoining sectors of Rohini Residential Scheme.
(ii) The LAC has failed to appreciate the land of the petitioners has great potential value.
The land in question has been notified for Rohini Residential Scheme, Phase III, under PDD.

Further the said land has great commercial value and the same is surrounded by fully LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 developed colony/ Rohini and also the fully developed industrial areas developed by the respondent no. 2.

sentences.text: (iii) The DDA has allotted flats, residential plots and commercial sites, which were developed by the DDA contractors and the same were sold by the DDA at very high prices.
The land of the petitioners is situated near the commercial sites, flats and residential plots.
The LAC would have issued/

served notices upon the petitioners then the petitioners would have certainly filed the claims and the relevant documents establishing the market value of the acquired land of the petitioners that the same was not less than Rs.
10,000/ per sq. yards.

(iv) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 5 crore per acre Rs. 10,000/ per sq. yard as on date of section 4 of the notification.

Further, it is prayed that statutory benefits like solatium, additional amount as well as the interests,
etc in addition the market value in terms of the provisions of LA Act.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/ Land Acquisition Collector (North West) and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the notification under Section 4 was passed on 04.06.2004 and the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 03.06.2005 and the said land has LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh & Ors. locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

The Ld. sentences.text: It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available LAC no. 17/
2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh & Ors.
Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 14 to Ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

11. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
12. It is submitted that the possession of the said land was transferred from L&B/ LAC to DDA on 22.08.2008.

It is submitted that the compensation passed by ld. LAC is legal, adequate, just and fair and the same has been awarded by ld. LAC after taking into consideration all the factors relevant for determining the compensation, as such the petitioner is not entitled for grant of enhancement of compensation.

All the other LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW)) Hukam Singh &
Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 14 averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition are denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is liable to be dismissed with cost.

17. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Randhir Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 21.11.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
18. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Pooth Kalan is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

20. In the case of Randhir Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Pooth Kalan acquired through Award LAC no. 17/ 2016 (Award No. 04/200607/DC(NW))

sentences.text: There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Randhir Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Randhir Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.22,20,900/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.6,50,900/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

An enhancement of Rs.6,50,900/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).

opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Randhir Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.22,20,900/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.6,50,900/ per acre.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.22,20,900/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.6,50,900/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
